Fixed structural features explicitly required by the contract are allowed."},"candidate_prose":"The wind shoved at Deniz as he hurried along the hill path, holding his kite firmly.

“I’ve got it,” he told Ece, though she had not said anything.

A stronger gust swept over the hill. The kite snapped out of Deniz’s hands, spun above the path, and sailed toward the footbridge.

“Hey!”

Deniz chased it with his eyes. The kite dipped, bounced once against the fixed railing, and caught there. It trembled wildly in the wind but stayed intact.

Deniz dashed toward the bridge. “I can reach it from here.”

Ece caught up, her scarf still clutched in her hands. “Not safely. Come down the lower bridge path. It leads to the bridge approach.”

“That takes longer.”

“It also keeps us off the railing.”

Deniz stared at his kite fluttering above them. Every gust made him want to rush straight after it. Then he glanced at the way Ece was pointing and gave a short, unhappy sigh.

“Fine. The lower path,” he said. “But quickly.”

Ece guided him along the lower bridge path, and Deniz followed, looking back whenever the kite flapped loudly. The wind kept racing across the hill, but the kite remained caught on the railing.

Together they reached the bridge approach. Deniz stopped there beside Ece, impatient but no longer charging ahead.

“All right,” he said, watching the kite. “We do this your way.”","deterministic_findings":[]}
